title: Customer Success: Game Day Simulation Playbook for Enterprise Onboarding
author: Priya Desai
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable, measurable game-day simulation designed to validate enterprise onboarding readiness for Redwood Inference customers. The exercise exercises critical success paths (go‑live, degraded throughput, model failover, networking incidents, and billing/quotas) and verifies cross-functional coordination between Customer Success, Support, SRE, and Engineering.

Goals:
- Verify end-to-end customer go-live checklist can be executed under stress.
- Validate monitoring & alerting triggers, escalation paths, and on-call handoffs.
- Surface integration edge cases (VPC networking, KMS access, streaming webhooks).
- Measure response time to simulated incidents and close the loop with concrete action items.
- Create repeatable artifacts: post‑game report, RCA action items, and knowledge base updates.

Audience and Scope:
- Primary audience: Customer Success Managers (CSM), Support Engineers, SRE oncall, Solutions Engineers, and customer's technical contacts.
- Scope: Enterprise Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted API smoke tests included when relevant.
- Out of scope: Model training jobs, billing disputes unrelated to onboarding config.

Prerequisites (must be completed before scheduling a game day):
1. Signed onboarding checklist present in the customer record (owner: CSM).
2. Dedicated or Private environment accessible to Redwood SRE and the customer's technical lead.
3. Test API keys and a sandbox model pinned to a known, small test-model (e.g., m-small-test-v1).
4. Observability access: dashboards shared, alert notification channels confirmed (PagerDuty, Slack channels).
5. Contact roster: primary/secondary oncall for customer, CSM, SE, SRE lead, and Support manager.
6. Pre-loaded test prompts and evaluation prompts for quality checks.

Schedule and Timebox:
- Total duration: 3.5 hours (recommended).
  - 00:00–00:30: Kickoff and validation of prerequisites.
  - 00:30–01:15: Planned scenario A (Go-live smoke + capacity ramp).
  - 01:15–02:00: Planned scenario B (Model failover + quantization mismatch).
  - 02:00–02:30: Planned scenario C (Network partition / VPC routing).
  - 02:30–03:00: Unplanned surprise scenario (simulated production alert).
  - 03:00–03:30: Debrief and immediate action items.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- CSM (owner): Coordinates schedule, confirms business objectives, communicates outcomes to customer stakeholders.
- Support Engineer (responder): Triage alerts, execute customer-facing mitigation steps, document steps in ticket.
- SRE (technical lead): Owns infrastructure actions (scaling, routing changes, failover), runs diagnostic queries.
- Solutions Engineer (integration lead): Validates config, manifests, and client SDK behavior.
- Incident Commander (rotating): Runs timeline, assigns tasks, ensures post-game deliverables.

Pre-built Scenarios (examples):
1) Scenario A — Controlled Go-live & Capacity Ramp
   - Objective: Validate autoscaling, rate-limit configs, and initial cost telemetry.
   - Steps:
     1. Switch customer from pre-production API key to go-live API key (SE verifies).
     2. Ramp request rate from 5 RPS to 200 RPS across 10 minutes using load script.
     3. Observe autoscaler behavior for Dedicated pool and record scale events.
     4. Verify token-level cost breakdown appears in Redwood Console and matches expected model units.
   - Success criteria: p95 latency under 350ms; autoscaler scales to expected instance count within target window; no 5xx spikes above 0.5%.

2) Scenario B — Model Variant Failover + Quantization Mismatch
   - Objective: Exercise model-router fallback and quality regression detection.
   - Steps:
     1. Intentionally introduce an incompatible quantization config on the primary model variant (simulate misconfigured model binary).
     2. Trigger a burst of inference that routes to the primary; observe fallback to a verified variant (fallback window: 30s).
     3. Run prompt set with key quality tests; alert if BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics drop beyond threshold.
   - Success criteria: Traffic reroutes to verified variant within 60s; quality monitoring detects regression and creates an evaluation ticket.

3) Scenario C — VPC Routing and KMS Latency Spike
   - Objective: Validate customer private networking and KMS access under intermittent latency.
   - Steps:
     1. Simulate increased latency to KMS (inject 300–700ms latency at the customer VPN boundary).
     2. Observe request timeouts, queuing behavior, and rate limiting.
     3. Run mitigation: enable local TTL-based KMS caching (if configured) and re-run traffic.
   - Success criteria: Reduced end-to-end failures after caching enabled; no customer data exposed in logs; SLO for request success maintained above 98% during simulated window.

4) Surprise Scenario — Observability Alert + Paging
   - Objective: Validate operator escalation flow, oncall handoff, and customer communication cadence.
   - Steps:
     1. Fire synthetic alert: p99 latency > 1.5x SLO for 5 minutes.
     2. Confirm PagerDuty page fires, escalation proceeds to the correct rotation.
     3. Incident Commander opens incident ticket, CSM crafts initial customer notification using template.
   - Success criteria: Page acknowledged within 5 minutes, incident communications sent within 15 minutes, runbook tasks initiated.

Execution Playbook (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff (CSM): Share agenda, objectives, and success criteria. Confirm observation points and who will own each scenario.
2. Baseline capture (SRE): Collect baseline dashboards (latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth) and snapshot logs.
3. Execute scenario (Incident Commander assigns tasks): Use validated scripts from /contrib/game-day-scripts. Capture timestamps for key events.
4. Immediate mitigation (Support / SRE): Apply documented mitigations; if not available, escalate to Engineering and note time-to-escalate.
5. Document (Support Engineer): Open post-game ticket with timestamps, logs, and screenshots.
6. Debrief (All): 15–30 minute structured debrief in which each role provides findings, blockers, and proposed fixes.
7. Post-game artifacts (CSM owner): Post a short report to customer record and update the knowledge base article referenced in the ticket.

Post-Game Report Template (must be completed within 48 hours):
- Executive summary (1 paragraph).
- Timeline of events (table with timestamps, actor, action).
- Metrics observed vs. expected (latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, instance counts).
- Root cause hypotheses and confirmed root cause (if any).
- Action items (owner, priority, ETA).
- Knowledge base updates (links).

Sample Timeline Table (ASCII):
| Time (UTC) | Actor | Event | Notes |
|------------|-------|-------|-------|
| 15:02 | Support | Customer switched to go-live key | SE verified config |
| 15:08 | SRE | Autoscaler triggered +3 nodes | scale latency 75s |
| 15:22 | SRE | Model failover initiated | fallback to variant v1-stable |

Metrics and SLOs to validate during game day:
- API success rate (2xx): target >= 99.0% during simulation window.
- p95 latency: target <= 350ms for short-form text models; p99 <= 800ms.
- Autoscaler reaction time: scale-up start < 120s after threshold breach.
- PagerDuty page-to-ack: < 5 minutes.
- Mean time to mitigation for mitigatable incidents: < 30 minutes.

Common failure modes and recommended mitigations:
- Failure mode: KV cache invalidation after model variant swap.
  - Mitigation: Warm caches using replay of peak traffic; pre-warm sequence cache for pinned variants.
- Failure mode: KMS timeouts in high-latency regions.
  - Mitigation: Enable regional KMS proxy and client-side retry/backoff.
- Failure mode: Misconfigured rate limits cause 429 storm.
  - Mitigation: Gradual ramp plan with automated throttling and synthetic traffic gating.

Artifacts and Repositories:
- Game-day traffic scripts: git@redwood:infra/game-day-scripts.git (branch: enterprise-onboarding).
- Templates: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-template-and-operational-checklist-2026.
- Runbooks referenced: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-process and /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollouts.

Communication Templates (short):
- Initial customer notification (15min):
  Hi <Customer Team>,
  We are conducting a scheduled verification exercise for your go‑live. You may see elevated traffic and controlled rollbacks during the window. We will keep you updated every 15 minutes.

- Incident status update (30min):
  Current status: Investigating elevated p99 latency. Impact: API errors for 2% of requests. Next update in 30 minutes. Owner: <SRE Lead>.

Debrief & Continuous Improvement:
- All post-game action items must be tracked in the customer onboarding Jira board and closed within 30 days (CSM owner).
- Quarterly re-run recommended for customers on Dedicated/Private who cross 10% month-over-month usage growth.
- Add new scenarios to the playbook when we encounter gaps; maintain change log in the page history.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets:
- Run load script (local):
  ./scripts/ramp_load.sh --api-key $TEST_KEY --rps 200 --duration 600

- Capture baseline traces (SRE):
  curl -sS "https://api.redwood.dev/metrics?env=staging&customer=<id>" | jq . > baseline.json

Appendix B — Known limitations:
- This playbook cannot safely simulate hardware failures (NVLink/GPU hang) in customer Dedicated pools without explicit engineering signoff.
- Some quality-monitoring thresholds are model-specific; coordinate with Applied ML to define correct pass/fail gates.

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: Customer Success (CSM Guild).
- Recommended review cadence: every 6 months or after any enterprise incident.
- Required reviewers: SRE Lead, Support Manager, Solutions Engineering Lead.

Contact & escalation list (short):
- CSM: priya.desai@redwood.ai
- Support Manager: support-manager@redwood.ai
- SRE Rotation (pager): +PD:eng-sre-oncall
- SE lead: se-lead@redwood.ai

End of playbook.
